candidates.attacker_control: Unauthenticated remote HTTP client controls the 'host' query parameter of GET /getFavicon on the admin console port (default 9090 HTTP / 9091 HTTPS, bound to all interfaces unless adminConsole.interface/network.interface is set). The value is concatenated into the outbound URL, so the attacker can supply host:port, a path, a query string, userinfo, or a hostname resolving to an internal address; Apache HttpClient follows redirects (LaxRedirectStrategy), so the final destination is also attacker-influenced.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified web.xml filter mappings (only *.jsp, PluginServlet, dwr-invoker are behind AuthCheckFilter; /getFavicon is not) and that web.xml contains no <security-constraint>; confirmed AdminConsolePlugin.createWebAppContext installs no extra security handler and getBindInterface() returns null (all interfaces) by default. Confirmed the scheme is hard-coded to http (no file:// or gopher://), which limits but does not prevent the attack. Timeouts (2s connect/socket) and the miss-cache (default icon after two failures) slow but do not stop targeted reads. Checked that this is reachable even before login; the admin console itself requires setup completion to start.
candidates.impact: Unauthenticated SSRF with response read-back: internal host/port scanning and retrieval of responses from HTTP services reachable from the Openfire host (cloud instance metadata/credentials, internal web admin panels, internal APIs). A successful 200 response body is returned to the attacker and additionally cached in the 'Favicon Hits' cache. This enables credential theft from metadata services and access to internal-only endpoints.
candidates.prerequisites: Network reachability to the admin console HTTP(S) listener (defaults to all interfaces, port 9090, enabled whenever the admin console is running). No credentials or session required. Non-default bind restrictions or a firewall in front of port 9090 reduce reachability.
candidates.root_cause: FaviconServlet.doGet reads the request parameter 'host' and passes it unchanged into getImage(host, defaultBytes), which builds the URL "http://" + host + "/favicon.ico" and executes it server-side with an Apache HttpClient configured with LaxRedirectStrategy; the response entity bytes are then written back to the requester. There is no allow-list, no private/loopback address rejection, no restriction to the admin console's own host, and no authentication: web.xml maps the servlet at /getFavicon but AuthCheckFilter is only mapped to *.jsp, PluginServlet and dwr-invoker, and the descriptor contains no <security-constraint>.
candidates.title: Unauthenticated SSRF in admin-console FaviconServlet via host parameter (/getFavicon)
candidates.trace: HTTP GET /getFavicon?host=<value> -> FaviconServlet.doGet (line 119) -> host normalized only by the gmail->google special case (line 121) -> getImage(host, defaultBytes) (line 123) -> getImage("http://" + host + "/favicon.ico") (line 164) -> RequestBuilder.get(url).setConfig(timeouts).build() (line 191) -> client.execute(getRequest) (line 195) -> EntityUtils.toByteArray(response.getEntity()) (line 197) -> writeBytesToStream(bytes, response) (line 125). Because the attacker can embed '?' in host, the fixed '/favicon.ico' suffix can be pushed into the query string, giving full control of the requested path (e.g., host=169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/<role>? requests that metadata path and returns its body).
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed (no execution permitted). Whether Jetty/HttpClient accept every crafted host value (e.g., embedded '?'/'#'/userinfo) was reasoned from source, not tested; the exact set of internal endpoints and cloud metadata availability depends on the deployment; cache behavior for oversized responses was not runtime-checked.

coverage_summary: Reviewed the Openfire 4.5.0-SNAPSHOT tree exposed in this run: 1031 visible files, 721 Java files parsed by the relation index (index status partial: syntax/containment/naming candidates only; 30,952 unresolved calls; no control-flow, data-flow, semantic resolution, or Spring runtime verification). Focused source review on externally reachable surfaces: admin-console web.xml filters/servlets (AuthCheckFilter, PluginServlet, FaviconServlet, PluginIconServlet, ResourceServlet, SystemProperties/SystemCacheDetails servlets, dwr.xml), HTTP/BOSH/WebSocket endpoints, XMPP stanza handlers (register/bind/private/vCard), auth and authorization (AuthFactory/AuthToken/AdminManager/DefaultAuthorizationPolicy/SCRAM), TLS/certificate handling (Server/ClientTrustManager, TrustStore, SASL EXTERNAL verification), file transfer/proxy, plugin loading (zip-slip checks), update manager, database providers (prepared statements, LDAP filter escaping), and utility crypto/encoding. Configuration and i18n/property files were consulted where relevant. No JSPs and no test sources exist in the snapshot, so server-side rendering and JSP-mediated flows (including login.jsp/loginToken.jsp and setup pages) could not be audited; XMPP protocol internals were sampled rather than exhaustively traced.
limitations: Findings are based on static source reading only; no code was executed and no runtime confirmation of reachability or exploitability was performed.

The P1 relation index is partial and syntactic: it has no data-flow, control-flow or semantic resolution, and 30,952 call sites are unresolved, so it cannot prove or disprove reachability; all index hints were verified against source text.

JSP files are absent from the snapshot, so web-app paths that depend on JSP logic (login.jsp, loginToken.jsp, setup/*.jsp, admin pages) and any XSS/redirect/CSRF issues in them are out of scope of this review.
No test sources are present; behavior assertions are inferred from code and configuration comments.

Runtime deployment factors (firewalling of the admin console port, adminConsole.interface binding, cloud-vs-on-prem hosting, presence of internal HTTP services) determine the real impact of the submitted SSRF candidate and were not verified.
Protocol-level XMPP handlers were sampled; a deeper review of MUC/pubsub/session code could surface additional issues not listed here.

rejected_leads.lead: WebDAVLiteServlet.isAuthorized (line 160) calls getOccupantsByBareJID(bareJID) but discards the result and returns true, so the MUC membership check is ineffective; path segments (service/room/file) are also concatenated into a file path without canonicalization (line 75).
rejected_leads.reason: The servlet is not registered anywhere in the snapshot (no web.xml servlet/servlet-mapping entry, no other reference), and its own comment says it is work-in-progress dead code ('checked in for future use'); no reachable attack path can be established, so it was not submitted.

rejected_leads.lead: PluginServlet.handleOtherRequest builds File(pluginDirectory, parts[1] + '/web' + contextPath) and handleDevJSP builds File(webDir, jsp) from request path info, which would permit path traversal if '..' reached the servlet.
rejected_leads.reason: Access is behind AuthCheckFilter (PluginServlet mapping) and requires admin rights; Jetty normalizes/rejects '..' path segments before servlet dispatch, and dev-mode JSP compilation additionally requires the plugin to be in development mode. Exploitability could not be established from source alone.

rejected_leads.lead: AuthCheckFilter.testURLPassesExclude allows URLs starting with 'setup/setup-' when they contain no '..' and no '%2e' (lines 158-164); an encoding-based bypass (CVE-2023-32315-style) could expose non-setup pages unauthenticated.
rejected_leads.reason: The JSPs that the exclude targets (setup/*.jsp, login.jsp, etc.) are not present in this snapshot, so no protected target reachable through this rule could be verified; no bypass of the '..'/percent-encoding checks could be demonstrated from the available files.

rejected_leads.lead: IQRegisterHandler allows an authenticated user to create additional accounts via the legacy two-element query form even when in-band registration is disabled (lines 326-362, onlyPassword path).
rejected_leads.reason: Matches the apparent upstream design (the branch is commented as intended for authenticated admins); requires an already-authenticated account and only creates accounts, so severity/impact is low and intent is uncertain.

rejected_leads.lead: ClientTrustManager.checkServerTrusted and ServerTrustManager.checkServerTrusted/checkClientTrusted perform no validation (lines 339-345 and 67-98), potentially allowing certificate spoofing on c2s/s2s.
rejected_leads.reason: Comments indicate validation is intentionally deferred to SASL EXTERNAL/dialback checks elsewhere; whether the deferred validation fully covers every path could not be proven from source in this review.

rejected_leads.lead: ProxyConnectionManager.activate matches transfers solely by SHA-1 digest of sid+initiator+target, allowing an entity that knows those values to hijack a SOCKS5 bytestream.
rejected_leads.reason: Long-standing protocol design; attacker knowledge of sid/initiator/target and impact could not be established from the available code alone.

rejected_leads.lead: Base64.decodeToObject performs Java deserialization of attacker-influencable input.
rejected_leads.reason: No caller of decodeToObject exists in the snapshot, so the sink is unreachable.

summary: Openfire 4.5.0-SNAPSHOT (XMPP server, Java). The strongest source-verified issue is an unauthenticated server-side request forgery in the admin-console FaviconServlet: GET /getFavicon?host=... makes the server fetch http://<attacker-supplied host>/favicon.ico with Apache HttpClient (redirects followed) and streams the response body back. The servlet is mapped at /getFavicon, and AuthCheckFilter in web.xml only covers *.jsp, PluginServlet and dwr-invoker, so no login/admin role is required. The host value is concatenated without any allow-list or address validation, so it can carry a port, path, query, or userinfo, letting the caller reach arbitrary internal HTTP services (including cloud metadata endpoints) and read their responses. Other candidate areas were reviewed and rejected/deferred (unregistered WebDAV servlet with an ignored authorization check, PluginServlet path construction behind admin auth, AuthCheckFilter wildcard-exclude traversal checks whose bypass could not be demonstrated, and several no-op/inconclusive TLS or transfer checks).
